The proof is in `/work/putnam_2012_b5.lean`. It compiles with exit 0, with no errors and no `sorry` warning. The imports, theorem statement, and file name are unchanged, and the file has no `sorry`, `axiom`, or `native_decide`.

Approach: with `a(s) = log g1(s)` and `b(s) = log g2(s)`, the left side is `sup_s exp(x·a(s) + b(s))`. Each term is a supremum of tangent lines of `exp`: `exp(y) = sup_c exp(c)·(1 + (y − c))`. So I index the affine family by pairs `(s, c)`. A cardinality argument gives an equivalence `ℝ ≃ ℝ × ℝ` to reindex it by a single real `t`. Then `h1` and `h2` are the slope and intercept of the tangent line for `(s, c)`. The two suprema are shown equal by mutual `csSup` inequalities, with `exp` bounded above using `g1, g2 ≤ B1, B2`.
